segment.source: ::She aims her rifle at you.::<end>
<end>
So... you're that corporal $(#guy/girl). <end>
Hm. We'll see...<end>
So... you're the new $(#guy/girl). <end>
<end>
This way, newbie!<end>
Get ready. They're coming...<end>
<end>
Move! You're messing up my aim.<end>
::Looks through the scope.::<end>
Frag the bastards!<end>
Worry about your own hide...<end>
Congratulations, you're alive. Now report to Chief Briggs.<end>
<end>
Fraggin' pirate scum...<end>
Fraggin' savages...<end>
::Tracks the rampaging Naga Protector through her scope.:: Can't get a clear fraggin' shot...<end>
Go and pack your bags. We're getting outta Hell's Gut.<end>
<end>
Good riddance. <end>
::She returns to scanning the dim horizon.::<end>
You shouldn't be here anymore. <end>
::Cold air surrounds the roof. Yahota stands still, gazing at the sea, her cloak flapping in the wind - which doesn't seem to bother her at all.::<end>

::She glances at you, but somewhat incompletely, as though allocating anything more than the edge of her peripheral vision to identify you is redundant.::
It's you. What is it?<end>
Hey there.<end>
::She nods, ::<end>
::her eyes scanning the vast gloomy sea.::<end>
<end>
I'm interested in enemy activity.<end>
The sea's looking calm at the moment. No enemy activity whatsoever.<end>
There was something else I wanted to ask you...<end>
Thanks for the info. I'll leave you to your duty.<end>
I'll leave you to your duty.<end>
Pirates or savages?<end>
Pirates.<end>
<end>
The whole south-eastern part of the sea is pretty much dead. Barely any pirate activity there.<end>
<end>
<end>
And the natives?<end>
<end>
Haven't noticed any activity lately. No moving lights, boats or anything of the sort. <end>
<end>
And the pirates?<end>
Not much activity lately. Much fewer moving lights and boats as well. <end>
This might be the calm before the storm.<end>
<end>
Less activity than before the first attack, but still plenty.<end>
Still lots of activity. There's a lot of them there. <end>
Lots of activity there ever since we moved in. They are probably preparing for another attack.<end>
Not much activity over at the pirate base. Their patrols are becoming rather sparse as well.<end>
Lots of pirate jet ski patrols about. They could be up to something<end>
again<end>
.<end>
Savages.<end>
Can you see the Ferryman anywhere?<end>
No. He sailed north into savage territory before I lost sight of him.<end>
But he should be in my scope again soon. <end>
He follows a fairly consistent route, visiting the mutie island and the pirate base before going north again.<end>
::She nods.:: He's docked at the <end>
pirate base. <end>
He's lying on the ground and doesn't appear to be moving. Looks fragged to me.<end>
pier on the southern side of the mutie island. <end>
What can you see from here?<end>
You got eyes as well...<end>
::[Perception] Look around.:: Let's put them to the test... Well, there's a... a spider, a giant spider on that island northwest of here, for instance.<end>

::She looks northwest without squinting.::
Yes, I see it. That's a... good catch.<end>
Still, I need some info on the surrounding locations and what is and has been going on around here.<end>
::She inhales and exhales slowly as her eyes are panning across the scenery.:: South, it's nothing but the Jaws, as you locals call it, <end>
and that glowing monolith on the cliff.<end>
West, mutie island, you already know. <end>
Saw no activity after you left.<end>
East and southeast, pirate territory: <end>
Little to no activity. <end>
North - <end>
now that's the... fraggin' savage land. <end>
<end>
Haven't noticed any activity lately. No moving lights or anything of the sort. <end>
North-east, <end>
that's where the horticulture center is located. You know all about that.<end>
<end>

::She pauses.:: There's also this guy cruising around on a crane ferry. Old man. Armed. Refused to cooperate. Could be a pirate, as I've seen him sail into their port on numerous occasions. I've also seen him go north into savage territory.<end>

::She falls silent for a moment.::
Gotta keep my eyes peeled at all times. It appears as though you can see a lot from here, but everything's a lot closer than you think. Gotta stay alert.<end>
::She turns away.::<end>
there's plenty of vegetation there. And some kind of... fraggin' mist, damned if I know what it is. Can't see much there, generally.<end>
Not much activity lately. Much fewer moving lights as well. <end>
This might be the calm before the storm.<end>
<end>
Less activity than before the first attack, but still plenty.<end>
Still lots of activity. There's a lot of them. <end>
Lots of activity there ever since we moved in. <end>
There's a few spots which are well-illuminated; that must be where their villages are.<end>
the savage land. <end>
Lots of activity after the attack.<end>
Lots of lights, lots of jets patrolling around. <end>
Also, the whole eastern side of the Black Sea is basalt rock, but there's also a lot of that red vegetation there.<end>
<end>
West, on that island, that's where the muties live. Not much activity there, generally.<end>
You've got better eyes than me.<end>
::She nods.::<end>
I need some info on the surrounding locations and what is and has been going on around here.<end>
I suppose I do.<end>
Of course you do.<end>
Just answer the damn question. I need information.<end>
Watch it.<end>
Tell me about the surrounding areas.<end>
South, it's the Jaws <end>
You don't seem very pleased with me being around.<end>
::She remains silent...::<end>
::...and continues staring at the sea.::<end>
Company is distraction. I don't like distractions.<end>
But you're alright, I guess.<end>
You're tolerable.<end>
But you fight well, so you're worth something. Guess I can tolerate you.<end>
Are you bothered by strange dreams as well?<end>
::She shakes her head...::<end>
No. I don't dream.<end>
You do sleep, right?<end>
::She glances at you.:: I sleep in short, one and a half hour phases. That's one full sleep cycle. Couple of times a day. Always have.<end>
If I do dream... ::She slowly shakes her head.:: I don't remember it.<end>
You mean, you don't sleep at all?<end>
I wanted to ask you about your relationship with Chief Briggs.<end>

::She gives you a cold stare.::
<end>
Bri--? ::She shakes her head.:: No. We won't be talking about the chief right now. <end>
No... C'mon. ::She turns to the sea.::<end>
What's there to ask?<end>
Are you his daughter? I mean, you both have that silent type persona about you, and you kinda even look alike.<end>
::Her frigid stare persists.::<end>

::And then she looks away.::
<end>
Damn, you got dumb questions. Fraggin' dumb.<end>
Are you related in any way? Some of us have noticed some... similarities.<end>
Are you two lovers? He asked to see you straight away after returning from Core City, and frankly, you do look like his type.<end>
Am I his... *what*...?<end>

::Her lips tighten. She moves toward you; you expect assault but instead she calmly leans forward and whispers into your ear...::
Richard Briggs is the chief of Aegis Incorporated and my commanding officer. Nothing more, nothing less. If you imply anything different one more time or spread any rumors, any rumors at all, you or anyone else, then know that I can easily hit a fast moving head full of *crap* out there where no one will know what happened.<end>
Listen, everyone's already talking about it.<end>
Really now? Are they?<end>
Outta my sight, fraggin' insect.<end>
<end>
With pleasure.<end>
Serpent.<end>
::Say nothing.::<end>
Mhm. I'll try not to.<end>
I won't.<end>

::She looks at you for a few more seconds.::
<end>
Sorry.<end>
::Say nothing.::<end>
Don't you threaten me, you featureless slag!<end>
Nothing.<end>
::She turns away.::<end>
Tell me about yourself.<end>
<end>

::She looks at you, sighing.::
What? What? I'm a sec-specialist currently on guard duty trying to keep us all alive, okay. I'd rather be moving around like usually but... frag it, it's what I gotta do.<end>

::She pauses.:: Look... I wanna be left alone. I work best *alone*: I can concentrate, I can think, I can plan my moves without depending on anyone else - and I got no attachments.
So let's keep things that way. You do your job, I'll do mine.<end>
::Silence ensues.::<end>
There's nothing to tell. I'm just a sec-specialist doing my job.<end>
::She gives you a freezing glance before returning to her duty.::<end>
Any final thoughts before we depart?<end>
No. No. Nothing besides what I've told you already.<end>
Don't know what I expected.<end>
::She turns toward you.::<end>
If you expected me to open my heart to you about how it's been difficult and how I'm lucky to be alive...<end>
::She looks you dead in the eye.:: Frag it, $(#man/sis), just frag it. Now go pack your bags and leave me alone.<end>
::She chuckles and returns to the sea.:: Damn, $(#man/sis). You and your questions.<end>
Well, it's been... interesting.<end>
Ah. You know, I think your attitude is the one freezing this rooftop, not the winds.<end>
::She frowns.:: <end>
::Nod.::<end>
Tell me about the monolith.<end>
::She answers coldly.:: <end>
Can't tell you much. Never seen anything like it before. It's a strange, glowing, angular structure.<end>

There is a human-shaped statue beside it. At first I thought it was a pirate, but it never moved. It's got something in its hands, but I can't tell what it is 'cause of the glow.
That's all I got for you.<end>
It's a lot colder up here. Where's all the warm air rising from below?<end>

::She nods.:: There's a cold air current coming down from that crevice up there. ::She points to a crevice in the cavern ceiling north of you. You can see some bats approaching it from the side and being carried off course some ten meters south.::<end>
And it's hitting just this fraggin' lighthouse.<end>
How good of a shot are you?<end>
::She nods...::<end>
Outstanding. <end>

::She glances at you::
<end>
Don't you have any surveillance and detection equipment you can use?<end>
::She answers coldly.:: <end>
NV and thermal cameras, auto-turrets, perimetral omnisensors and other automatic detection systems. We brought it all.<end>
Then why not install some of that up here?<end>

::She scans the sea from east to west.:: The Hell's Gut is too busy a place; the automatics get confused, start false alarms. Cannot be entirely relied upon.
Cameras, they require keen human eyes behind them.<end>

Mine are the keenest around here; all the optical equipment I'll ever need is this scope.
::She looks at it, then through it as she carries on with her duty.::<end>
I need some information.<end>
Just checking up on you.<end>
We're all going to be here for a while, so why not get to know each other a bit better.<end>
::She says nothing, ::<end>
I wanted to compliment you on your fighting abilities.<end>
Guess it's time to leave this place. <end>
::She continues staring at the sea.::<end>
And we even... even got a live Lemurian out of it. ::She shakes her head in disbelief.:: <end>
It's been too fraggin' long...<end>

::Her presence feels colder than the winds whipping the rooftop.::
What?<end>

::She scans the sea and counts her bullets simultaneously, moving them from one satchel to the other. After reaching in the former for more and retrieving nothing, she closes the latter one and exhales softly, staring beyond the dim horizon.::<end>
<end>
I gotta hand it to you, you got the professor back without bloodshed. I wouldn't have the patience.<end>
Smooth negotiating there.<end>
Things got out of hand.<end>
::She nods.:: They surely did.<end>
::She turns toward the sea.::<end>
Did I ask for your opinion?<end>
You're getting it anyway. I did save your ass out there. You're welcome.<end>
Thanks for busting us out of there.<end>
::She nods.:: All in a day's work. <end>
I came here for some information.<end>
Go for it. <end>
::Say nothing.::<end>
The professor's back, and if we do our job right, hopefully not out of the pan and into the fraggin' fire.<end>

::She tracks the Naga Protector patrolling the beach through her scope.::
I don't trust bots. But then again...<end>
I could see your encounter with the turrets in front of that military installation at F12<end>
and the savage party's arrival after that. They occupy a lighthouse in D10. Think that's where you've been spotted from.<end>
. <end>
::She scans the dim horizon, occassionally looking through her scope when details require closer examination.:: <end>
<end>
I gotta hand it to you, you saved all our asses. Had the pirates succeeded at the Keep, we'd be in a world of hurt right now. ::She pauses.:: This way... we got the jump on them.<end>
::This time, however, she appears to be looking through it all.::<end>
Not many of us remaining. ::She looks at you as if she wants to continue but then turns away.::<end>
Doc bought it. Spared him the misery, if anything.<end>
How painters can stand to watch something as boring as this for hours and hours is something I'll never know. <end>
Ever seen a sea serpent eating a bat? The bat was flying low... then boom. Gone.<end>
You got us in. ::She nods.:: <end>
And fragged all the muties. <end>
Keep it up.<end>
